## Findings ledger
- [D4.DOC6.F3] Riley qualifies the reported Weberian interpretive strategy by noting that Biernacki gives relatively little account of the procedures by which interpretation is to be conducted — dim: citation_stance — ref: RW0021 — stance: qualifies — object: The return to Weberian ideal-type interpretation requires a more explicit procedure for cultural sociology — anchor: "But Biernacki says relatively little about procedures of interpretation." — doc: em:C9LPBLYH — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

sections_inspected: Back to Weber!, pp. 627–629, especially the sections “Two Sorts of Critique” and “Assessment”
scope_outcomes.criterion: A passage must express the citing author’s adoption, development, qualification, dispute, or explicit mention of a proposition attributed to Weber.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected text explicitly attributes propositions concerning Weber’s ideal types and interpretive method, qualifies the procedures offered for that method, and disputes Biernacki’s assimilation of Foucault to Weber.
limitations: The findings concern this supplied source only and do not establish Riley’s stance across his complete work.
Several Weber-related propositions are reported through Biernacki rather than quoted directly from Weber.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: Findings lost anchor evidence; this does not establish absence
One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
